title: Embedding Models Measure in Peculiar Ways
why_read: A focused empirical study showing that text embedding spaces poorly capture real physical measurements like mass and distance, relying instead on surface string similarity.
analysis: The paper investigates whether embedding models, which convert text into vectors used for similarity search and retrieval, actually understand physical quantities such as mass, distance, time, and volume in a consistent, objective way. They find embeddings only weakly capture true physical measurement relationships, and instead the vectors are heavily swayed by superficial similarities in how the numbers or units are written as strings rather than their real-world meaning. They also show that simple recalibration attempts don't fix this misalignment. This is a useful cautionary result for anyone building retrieval or search systems that assume embeddings encode numeric or physical facts correctly.
